REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - MARCH 22, 2018 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
MARCH 22, 2018, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was led by Pastor Carl Bernal from St. John Lutheran Church,
  Cerritos.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Elsus Camp Fire Club and Wakin Yo Lo Gidi
  Fire Club.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations

  Proclamations were presented to:

  Friends of the Cerritos Library ($15,000 contribution for RFID System).

  American Red Cross (Recognition of March 2018 as Red Cross Month).

  California Panel and Veneer Company (Business Spotlight).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  David Pylman stated his interest in the operations of the City Council, refining
  public policy, and detailed his qualifications and personal background. He
  expressed concerns with the City’s parking policy and Metro’s proposed rail
  project.

  John Paul Drayer spoke regarding various safety issues in the community,
  including homeless living hear Coyote Creek, and inquired how the City and
  School District can provide additional school safety measures. He commented
  on current litigation involving the Cerritos College Board.

  Mel Cortez thanked the City Council for their efforts, inquired as to the status
  of an official City of Cerritos Facebook page, and reported graffiti in the various
  areas.

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  A recommendation by the Cerritos Planning Commission, on a vote of 5-0, to forward
  the following to the City Council for their consideration:

  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AMENDING THE CERRITOS GENERAL PLAN LAND USE MAP
  BY CHANGING THE LAND USE DESIGNATION OF APPROXIMATELY ±1.98 ACRES OF
  LAND, LOCATED AT 12616 183RD STREET (APN 7030-002-902), FROM PUBLIC AND
  QUASI PUBLIC TO OFFICE PROFESSIONAL COMMERCIAL, HEREIN REFERENCED AS
  GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT 2017-1.*

  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and introduce AN ORDINANCE OF
  THE CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING THE CERRITOS DEVELOPMENT MAP BY
  CHANGING THE ZONE CLASSIFICATION OF APPROXIMATELY ±1.98 ACRES OF LAND,
  LOCATED AT 12616 183RD STREET (APN 7030-002-902), FROM OPEN SPACE (OS)
  TO COMMERCIAL OFFICE PROFESSIONAL (COP), HEREIN REFERENCED AS
  DEVELOPMENT MAP AMENDMENT 2017-2.(COUNCIL)*

  *Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA), this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Torrey Contreras, Director of Public Works.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments. Noting there were no
  individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments and the public
  hearing.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to table this item
  indefinitely (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  WAREHOUSING AND RELATED OFFICE USES AT 10637 MIDWAY AVENUE,
  CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703.  THE SUBJECT PROPERTY IS ZONED
  INDUSTRIAL COMMERCIAL-TWO (MC-2) (APN 7016-005-010) (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of implementation of traffic signal phasing
  modifications to the existing traffic signal at the intersection of Carmenita Road

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  David Pylman expressed concern with how the signal is activated.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor
  closed the public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to implement

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who

9D.  Review and consideration of award of Bid No. 1333-18, Printing of the Cerritos

  A staff report was given by Laurie Kajiwara, Public Information Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Noting there were no individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed the

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Award Bid No. 1333-18, Printing of the Cerritos Center for the Performing

  $108,575.04; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute changes in the
